title: Incident inventory & on-call bullet journal - May 11 2027
content:
Purpose: quick capture of this week's SRE incidents, SLO snapshot, on-call handoff notes, and outstanding runbook gaps. Informal, choppy — used for async catch-up and to seed follow-ups.

Summary bullets (top-level):
- Week: 2027-05-03 -> 2027-05-10 (shift rotation cover: APAC->EMEA->NA)
- Incidents: 3 user-facing degradations (one partial, two mitigated internally), 2 internal infra alerts (OOM, degraded autoscaler).
- SLOs: small p95 latency drift during Tue/Thu peak windows, error rate bump on Wed due to model-v2 rollout routing bug.
- Action items: short-term mitigations done; medium-term: runbook changes, improved canary gating, autoscaler thresholds review.

INCIDENT INVENTORY (short):
1) ID: JIRA-6789 / "Generation tail-latency spike" — 2027-05-04 09:22 UTC
   - Symptom: p95 token time spiked from baseline 210ms -> 1.1s for ~17m. Clients experienced delayed streams but no 5xxs.
   - Root cause hypothesis: cache-eviction thrash in host-mem layer when prefix cache reached GC boundary (observed correlated KV-cache churn).
   - Mitigation: reverted a recent micro-optimizing change in the batching service (roll back PR 1425), temporarily reduced batch_size_max to lower memory pressure.
   - Owners: Marco (lead responder), Asha (verification), Eve (telemetry).
   - Follow-ups: formal runbook for cache-eviction scenarios (see linked confluence), add cache-usage alert at 80% not 95%, schedule postmortem.

2) ID: JIRA-6792 / "Dedicated pool OOM cascade" — 2027-05-06 03:11 UTC
   - Symptom: Dedicated GPU pool reported repeated pod restarts, autoscaler eventually scaled up then flapped. Some customers on Dedicated saw brief 429s.
   - Root cause: rare quantization regression in new model variant causing larger-than-expected KV cache footprint; combined with aggressive pre-warming, nodes hit GPU memory limits.
   - Mitigation: paused rollout for that model variant, isolated variant to smaller instance group, applied node-level oom-killer soft limits.
   - Owners: Julian (mitigation), infra team (node limits).
   - Follow-ups: testing harness for quantization memory regressions, improve canary traffic profile (more realistic sequence lengths).

3) ID: JIRA-6801 / "Routing fallback misfire during canary" — 2027-05-07 14:05 UTC
   - Symptom: Canary policy mis-evaluated quality metric; automatic fallback engaged even though latency and error metrics were fine -> caused extra cold starts for some routes.
   - Root cause: misaligned threshold in rollout evaluator: quality metric used a stale embeddings baseline.
   - Mitigation: temporarily paused autonomous fallback; manually pinned routes to stable model; pushed quick patch to evaluator to ignore stale baselines.
   - Owners: product-hosted-api (lead), Asha (co-ordination).
   - Follow-ups: add integration test that simulates stale baseline scenario; add warning to console when baseline age > 6h.

INTERNAL ALERTS / OBSERVATIONS:
- Autoscaler jitter noted 2027-05-05 22:00 UTC: rapid up/down twice in one hour for region-us-west-2. Hypothesis: metric smoothing window too small for bursty inference workloads. Action: bump smoothing window from 30s -> 120s, monitor. Owner: infra.
- Latency regression pattern: p95 drift in late-night APAC window tied to longer prompt lengths from partner integration. Suggest adding length-aware routing (send longer sequences to larger-context pools). Owner: SRE + Platform eng.

SLO SNAPSHOT (quick):
- Hosted API availability (internal rolling): 99.95% (7d lookback) — within SLA but trending down 0.02% vs prior week.
- p95 generation latency (global): 230ms baseline; observed 270ms peak Wed-Thu.
- Error rate (5xx) hosted: 0.043% weekly. Spike Wed -> 0.17% coincided with model-v2 rollout.
- Notes: need to surface token-cost vs latency tradeoff in console for customers doing small prompts at high QPS.

ON-CALL HANDOFF NOTES (incoming -> outgoing):
- For incoming: verify rolling-change list in #infra-rollouts, check the last 12h increased-cache-usage alert (rule: cache-kv-usage > 80% for 5m).
- When handing off: paste the active incident IDs, current mitigations, and any TODOs in the handoff thread.
- Escalation path reminder: primary on-call -> infra pager (pg: infra-leads) -> SRE manager if >45m without mitigation.
- Pager etiquette reminder: always include playback bullet: what I tried, observed results, next step. Saves time at 3am.

RUNBOOK GAPS / TODOs (opportunities):
- Missing: explicit playbook for "prefix cache thrash" (high priority).
- Missing: quantization memory regression checklist in model-onboarding runbook.
- Improve: autopager duty script that includes recent PRs touching batcher/runtime.
- Add: synthetic canary that exercises long-sequence path (>=2048 tokens) on each deploy.

ACTION ITEMS (owners and ETA):
- Marco: Draft cache-eviction runbook v0.1 by 2027-05-17.
- Julian + infra: implement node-level soft-limits and validate for Dedicated pools — 2027-05-20.
- Eve: telemetry dashboard improvement (add baseline-age metric + alert) — 2027-05-18.
- Asha: schedule postmortem doc for JIRA-6789, kick off async writeup by 2027-05-14.

MEETING NOTES / Discussion snippets from weekly ops sync (2027-05-10):
- "Need better canary gating for model memory footprint — current metrics only look at latency & errors, not memory." — infra
- "Customers see spiky cost when we fall back to bigger variants; route economics should be visible per-route." — product
- "Consider prefix-aware batching heuristics: batch only if prefix matches cached vectors." — serving-runtime

OPEN QUESTIONS (to triage):
- How often do our canaries sample long-sequence examples? (need audit)
- What's the current false-positive rate on the cache-usage alert? (telemetry)
- Are there any customers still on the paused quantized variant? (CS check)

Notes to self / roughs:
- Keep handoff thread template: incident, short timeline, mitigation, next steps, owner, ETA. Paste every handoff.
- Remember to run postmortem template (no blame) and include capacity/cost impacts (token cost delta during incident).

References / links: JIRA-6789 (latency spike), JIRA-6792 (OOM cascade), CONFLUENCE runbook stub (cache-eviction), PR-1425 rollback.

End of page — short, actionable, will convert into formal postmortem + runbook stubs next week.

Quick sign-off: Asha (SRE rotation lead)
